summary: The root مَحَلَ (maḥala) implies striving or laboring to acquire something, often property, possibly without direct payment or through skillful management. It suggests an effortful pursuit.
lane: 5 تَمَحَّلْتُ مَالًا بِغَيْرِ ثَمَنٍ ذ I laboured to acquire property without price: (Msb:) or, accord. to Az, تَمَحَّلَ مَالًا means he laboured, and exercised art or management, in seeking [ to acquire ] property. (TA.) See also تَعَلَّثَ .

headwords.def: أَمْحَلَتِ النُّجُومُ The stars set aurorally and brought no rain. (S, K * in art. خوى.)

تَمَحَّلْتُ مَالًا بِغَيْرِ ثَمَنٍ I laboured to acquire property without price: (Msb:) or, accord. to Az, تَمَحَّلَ مَالًا means he laboured, and exercised art or management, in seeking [ to acquire ] property. (TA.) See also تَعَلَّثَ.
مَحْلٌ Drought, or suspension of rain, (S, K, Msb in art. جدب,) and dryness of the earth (S, Msb ubi suprà) depriving it of herbage; (S, TA;) and i. q. جَدْبٌ. (K.)
مَحَالَةٌ محال محاله محالة محل: see art. حول; and see also فَوْهَآءُ voce أَفْوَهُ, and فَوْقَآءُ voce أَفْوَقُ, and قَبٌّ.
لَبَنٌ مُمَحَّلٌ Sour milk upon which much fresh is milked: see قَارِصٌ.

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
